title: Record month, CEO celebrating a new logistics contract
text:
Session 7. Mood as logged: Positive.

Summary: The CEO opened by sharing a record month: two new logistics contracts signed and margin up four points. The ops lead reported the new dispatch system is live and on-time delivery rose to 96%. The team closed three of the four commitments from last session. The coach and CEO spent the second half planning the Q2 offsite.

Key issue: Sustaining delivery quality while onboarding the new contracts.

Commitments set this session (3):
- CEO to book the Q2 offsite venue by Friday
- Ops lead to share on-time delivery report weekly
- CEO to interview two dispatch supervisor candidates

Coach's notes on people:
- CEO (decision-maker): confidence up: energised by the contract wins and clear on priorities. ROI perception steady: credits the coaching for the pricing change that won the deal.
- Ops lead: momentum up: delivered the dispatch rollout on schedule.

title: Upbeat review, but the CFO questions what coaching is delivering
text:
Session 8. Mood as logged: Positive.

Summary: A friendly review of Q1 numbers. The CEO was upbeat and joked through most of the session. Near the end the CFO asked whether the coaching budget should be reviewed at the next board meeting, saying she could not point to anything that had changed in finance since January. The CEO moved on quickly.

Key issue: Q1 close and board preparation.

Commitments set this session (4):
- CFO to prepare board pack by the 28th
- CEO to confirm the offsite agenda
- Ops lead to send updated capacity plan
- CEO and CFO to agree Q2 hiring budget

Coach's notes on people:
- CEO (decision-maker): chemistry steady: warm and engaged throughout.
- CFO: ROI perception down: openly questioned the value of coaching and said finance had seen no change since January. Chemistry down: short answers and arms-length with the coach.

title: Founder agrees to four new initiatives while covering two open roles
text:
Session 12. Mood as logged: Positive.

Summary: The founder is enthusiastic about the growth plan and agreed to lead four new initiatives this quarter: a second clinic site, a patient app, a referral partnership and a new pricing model. She is also still covering the practice manager and head of billing roles, both open since November. She said she is working most weekends but 'it's temporary'.

Key issue: Choosing which growth initiatives to fund in Q1.

Risks raised: Founder burnout; Billing backlog

Commitments set this session (11):
- Founder to shortlist second-site locations
- Founder to brief the app agency
- Founder to draft referral partner terms
- Founder to model new pricing tiers
- Founder to interview practice manager candidates
- Founder to clear the billing backlog
- Founder to review Q1 budget
- Clinical lead to update rota
- Founder to meet the bank about a credit line
- Founder to finalise staff handbook
- Founder to send investor update

Coach's notes on people:
- Founder (decision-maker): implementation capacity down: covering two vacant roles and working weekends; nothing from last session's list was finished. Chemistry up: very open with the coach and grateful for the support.

title: Founder cut the list to three priorities and hired a practice manager
text:
Session 13. Mood as logged: Mixed.

Summary: The founder hired a practice manager, who starts next month, and agreed with the coach to park the app and pricing projects until Q3. She was tired but relieved. The billing backlog is half cleared. The clinical lead raised a staffing gap on Saturdays that was not resolved.

Key issue: Focusing the founder on three priorities while the new manager ramps up.

Commitments set this session (3):
- Founder to finalise second-site shortlist
- Practice manager onboarding plan drafted by founder
- Clinical lead to propose Saturday rota options

Coach's notes on people:
- Founder (decision-maker): implementation capacity up: the hire takes two roles off her plate next month. Confidence up: clearer after cutting the list.
- Clinical lead: momentum steady.

title: Strong sales month; the COO was quiet and asked to skip the next session
text:
Session 21. Mood as logged: Positive.

Summary: Sales beat target by 12% and the CEO praised the team. The COO, usually the most active voice, said very little, gave one-word answers when asked about the warehouse move, and asked whether she could skip the next session because she was 'not sure what she is getting out of these right now'. The CEO did not pick this up.

Key issue: Planning the warehouse move for Q3.

Commitments set this session (5):
- COO to confirm warehouse lease terms
- CEO to approve Q3 marketing budget
- Head of sales to share pipeline review
- COO to draft move timeline
- CEO to schedule leadership offsite

Coach's notes on people:
- CEO (decision-maker): confidence up: buoyed by the sales result.
- COO: engagement down: one-word answers and asked to skip the next session. ROI perception down: said she is not sure what she is getting out of the coaching. Coachability down: pushed back on every suggestion.

title: Coach met the COO one-to-one; she re-committed to the warehouse plan
text:
Session 22. Mood as logged: Neutral.

Summary: The coach held a one-to-one with the COO before the team session. She explained she felt sidelined in leadership meetings. Together they agreed she will own the warehouse move end to end and present it to the board. In the team session she was engaged again and led the discussion.

Key issue: Rebuilding the COO's ownership of the warehouse move.

Commitments set this session (2):
- COO to present the warehouse plan to the board on June 3
- CEO to give the COO decision rights on the move budget

Coach's notes on people:
- COO: engagement up: led the team discussion. ROI perception up: said the one-to-one was 'the most useful hour this year'.
- CEO (decision-maker): coachability steady: agreed to hand over the budget decision.

title: Owner signs two projects, then adds nine new to-dos for himself
text:
Session 30. Mood as logged: Positive.

Summary: The owner signed two large projects and is excited about the pipeline. He is still personally estimating every bid, approving every purchase order over $500 and running site walks, and said he cannot find time for the hiring plan agreed three sessions ago. The coach suggested delegating estimating; the owner said nobody else can do it properly yet.

Key issue: Scaling the business without the owner in every decision.

Risks raised: Owner bottleneck on estimating and approvals

Commitments set this session (9):
- Owner to estimate the hospital bid
- Owner to review PO approval thresholds
- Owner to write the estimator job description
- Owner to walk the two new sites
- Owner to meet the bonding agent
- Owner to finalise subcontractor list
- Owner to update cash-flow forecast
- Project manager to schedule kick-offs
- Owner to call the architect about change orders

Coach's notes on people:
- Owner (decision-maker): implementation capacity down: approving everything personally and the hiring plan has slipped for three sessions. Chemistry steady: trusts the coach. ROI perception steady: values the sessions.

title: Routine progress check, everything on schedule
text:
Session 31. Mood as logged: Positive.

Summary: A short progress check. Both new projects kicked off on time. The estimator role is posted and there are two strong applicants. The owner delegated PO approvals under $5,000 to the project manager. No new issues raised.

Key issue: Keeping the two new projects on schedule.

Commitments set this session (2):
- Owner to interview the two estimator applicants
- Project manager to report weekly on both projects

Coach's notes on people:
- Owner (decision-maker): implementation capacity up: delegated PO approvals and freed up two hours a day. Momentum up: hiring plan finally moving.
- Project manager: confidence up: pleased with the new approval authority.

title: CEO says the coaching feels expensive after a slow quarter
text:
Session 5. Mood as logged: Mixed.

Summary: Revenue came in 15% under plan. The CEO said that with cash tight he is 'looking hard at every line, including this one', and asked the coach what concrete result they could point to from the first four sessions. He was polite but guarded, and cut the session short by twenty minutes.

Key issue: Responding to a revenue shortfall.

Risks raised: Cash runway under six months; Coaching renewal at risk

Commitments set this session (4):
- CEO to review cost lines with the finance lead
- Head of sales to rebuild Q2 forecast
- CEO to decide on two open hires
- Finance lead to model a six-month runway scenario

Coach's notes on people:
- CEO (decision-maker): ROI perception down: questioned what the coaching has delivered so far. Chemistry down: guarded and ended the session early. Coaching affordability down: cash is tight.
- Finance lead: momentum steady.

title: Coach tied the pricing change to a $40k win; CEO renews
text:
Session 6. Mood as logged: Positive.

Summary: The coach opened with a value review: the pricing change agreed in session 3 produced a $40k upsell this month. The CEO said that was the proof he needed and confirmed the coaching renewal for another six months. The team agreed to focus Q2 on two enterprise deals.

Key issue: Closing two enterprise deals in Q2.

Commitments set this session (3):
- Head of sales to send proposals to both enterprise prospects
- CEO to join the second-round calls
- Finance lead to share weekly cash report

Coach's notes on people:
- CEO (decision-maker): ROI perception up: credited the pricing change and renewed. Chemistry up: relaxed and open again.
- Head of sales: confidence up: two strong enterprise leads.

title: Plant expansion on track; VP of ops overloaded but upbeat
text:
Session 17. Mood as logged: Positive.

Summary: The plant expansion is on schedule and the CEO is pleased. The VP of operations is running the expansion, the ERP migration and the food-safety audit at the same time. She said she is fine but admitted she has not taken a day off in two months. The team set a long list of follow-ups.

Key issue: Delivering the plant expansion, ERP migration and audit in the same quarter.

Risks raised: Key-person dependency on the VP of operations

Commitments set this session (8):
- VP ops to finalise equipment delivery schedule
- VP ops to run ERP data migration test
- VP ops to prepare audit documentation
- CEO to approve additional line staff
- VP ops to update the expansion budget
- Quality manager to run mock audit
- VP ops to sign off new supplier contracts
- CEO to meet the bank on expansion financing

Coach's notes on people:
- CEO (decision-maker): confidence up: expansion on track. ROI perception steady.
- VP of operations: implementation capacity down: running three major projects with no days off. Momentum steady: still hitting dates for now. Chemistry steady.

title: Audit finding and ERP delay; CEO frustrated with the team, not the coach
text:
Session 18. Mood as logged: Negative.

Summary: The food-safety audit raised a minor finding and the ERP go-live slipped two weeks. The CEO was frustrated and tense. He thanked the coach for pushing last session to add line staff, which he said kept the expansion on track, and asked for help restructuring the operations team so the VP of ops is not carrying three projects alone.

Key issue: Recovering from the audit finding and ERP delay.

Commitments set this session (3):
- CEO to appoint an ERP project owner separate from the VP of ops
- Quality manager to close the audit finding within 30 days
- CEO and coach to design the new ops structure next session

Coach's notes on people:
- CEO (decision-maker): confidence down: rattled by the audit and ERP slip. ROI perception up: credited the coaching for the staffing call and asked for more help. Chemistry up: leaned on the coach.
- VP of operations: implementation capacity down: still stretched, relief coming from the new ERP owner.
